events.title: Birth of Julius Caesar (traditional date)
events.description: Gaius Julius Caesar, the Roman general, statesman, and dictator, is traditionally said to have been born on July 12 (or 13) in 100 BCE. He rose to power through military conquests in Gaul and a civil war against Pompey and the Senate.
events.significance: Caesar's career and assassination helped end the Roman Republic and paved the way for the Roman Empire under his adopted heir Augustus. Note: the year is 100 BCE.

events.title: Battle of the Boyne (Gregorian date)
events.description: Protestant King William III of Orange defeated the deposed Catholic King James II near the River Boyne in Ireland. The battle was fought July 1, 1690 in the Julian calendar, which corresponds to July 11 in the Gregorian calendar, and is commemorated by Ulster Protestants on July 12.
events.significance: The victory secured the Protestant succession in Britain and Ireland and is still commemorated annually by the Orange Order with 'The Twelfth' celebrations in Northern Ireland.

events.title: Birth of Henry David Thoreau
events.description: Henry David Thoreau, American essayist, poet, and philosopher, was born in Concord, Massachusetts. He authored 'Walden' and 'Civil Disobedience'.
events.significance: Thoreau's writings on simple living, nature, and nonviolent resistance to unjust government influenced figures such as Gandhi and Martin Luther King Jr. and shaped American environmentalism.

events.title: The Rolling Stones perform their first concert
events.description: The Rolling Stones played their first public show at the Marquee Club in London, billed as 'The Rollin' Stones', with a lineup including Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Brian Jones, Ian Stewart, Dick Taylor and Mick Avory.
events.significance: The performance marked the start of one of the longest-lasting and most influential rock bands in history.

events.title: Kiribati gains independence
events.description: The Gilbert Islands, in the central Pacific Ocean, became independent from the United Kingdom as the Republic of Kiribati.
events.significance: The event was part of the late 20th-century wave of decolonization and created a new Pacific island nation.
